tOverview.text: Plotbreak v2 · make the app feel alive

nums.text:
The numbers behind the board (Nov 21, docs/retention-push-2026-11-21.md)
30 installs a day, 25 sign in, 12.6 ever play a turn. D1: 11% reopen, 7.6% play again. D7 any-open: 3.6%. 38% of people who finish onboarding never start a story. The free credits run out at exactly turn 10.

tHome.text: 1 · Home: a shelf that changes every day

h1.text:
1 · Continue goes above Featured
A returning player first sees their own unfinished run and the line it stopped on. Today Continue sits below the Tower card and the banner. Only 7.6% of players play again on day 1 (11% reopen); the cliffhanger line is the reason to tap.

h2.text:
2 · Featured: six slots, new every day, best openers first
Slots 1-2 are pinned from Good Morning Husband, Pink Tide, Zero Throne and Hush House; 3-6 rotate daily. Today Featured opens on Last Feather then Itachi, the two worst openers: 37% and 43% of first runs take a turn, against 67% for Pink Tide and 64% for Good Morning Husband.

h3.text:
3 · New on Plotbreak, then Hot right now
New: newest first, NEW badge for 7 days. Hot: most played in the last 72 hours. Today "Trending now" is lifetime plays, so it never moves. Renamed from "Trending now", which is OOC's row name.

h4.text:
4 · Three genre rows that change daily
Drawn from categories with 8+ worlds (mystery 25, action 21, school 15, romance 13, adventure 13, fantasy 12, drama 8). Worlds the player already started sink to the end of every row (Itachi, dimmed, in Mystery).

h5.text:
5 · Rising from the community
Player-made worlds ordered by plays this week, with the creator's name. Titles, creators and run counts here are production values. Creators who watch themselves climb come back to check (Create, note 3).

h6.text:
Daily claim on Home, turns in the header
The 300 daily credits (about 5 turns) hide in Wallet today. One-tap claim strip under Continue, streak and turns left in the header.

hA.text:
A · First week: Welcome missions fill the Continue slot
5 steps for 1,500 credits; step 4 only unlocks after midnight: "Come back tomorrow". OOC does the same: 500 credits at sign-up plus a Welcome Mission checklist on Home. Shown only in a player's first 7 days.

hB.text:
B · Later phase, not in feed/daily-freshness
Top 10 with a midnight reset, Moments from other runs, and Meet them (cast portraits). OOC resets its rankings daily and reshuffles two creator rows on every load.

hC.text:
C · The grid goes last
Today "All worlds" is an endless 3-column wall that starts on the first scroll. Move it to the bottom with a sort (Most played / Newest).

hD.text: Data note: titles, creators, plays and run counts come from production /v1/discover. Hot-row counts, Featured slots 3-6 and the Continue lines are illustrative. Show any live count only above a floor (e.g. 50) so a quiet day never reads as dead.

hE.text: OOC for scale: about 505 new stories went up on Nov 21 alone. Daily rankings, a 300/day check-in, and a Free Messages event with 7 free messages on every unplayed Original.

tDetail.text: 2 · Story detail: sell it in one screen

d1.text:
1 · Art first, full bleed
Key art fills the top ~45% and the title is set as a title card. Today the cover is a small thumbnail in an empty field under a "Story Information" header that reads like a settings page.

d2.text:
2 · Proof before the pitch
Plays, likes, comments and this week's rank sit directly under the title (OOC detail). The 2.9M / 157K numbers exist today but sit below six paragraphs of premise.

d3.text:
3 · Choose who you are, here
The archetypes move from the separate "What kind of Itachi are you?" page onto the detail page as cards. Picking one is a small commitment, and Play goes straight into the opener: one screen fewer between interest and the first beat.

d4.text:
4 · Read the first line before you play
The opening line in serif, then a collapsed premise. The current page leads with ~400 words of setup; the first line of the story is the strongest hook we own.

d5.text:
5 · What other players did
A first-choice split and the top comment: curiosity plus proof that people play this. Needs a small aggregate over turns; hide until a story has 50+ runs.

d6.text:
6 · Related worlds is real now
The server ranks it by shared categories, then 7-day plays (feed/daily-freshness). Half the new players who open a story page back out; this row gives them somewhere to go other than Home.

p1.text:
1 · A scene card on each new beat
A 16:9 image with place and time. OOC's play screen leads with art; ours is a wall of serif text from beat 2 on. The opener already proves the art exists; carry it into the feed.

p2.text:
2 · Speakers have faces
Dialogue carries the speaker's portrait and name, visual-novel style. The cast becomes people you recognise instead of quote marks.

p3.text:
3 · Suggestions you can edit
Three next moves, each with Edit and Send (OOC, Talkie). 11/22 churned players stalled in slow inspect/ask loops and 58-66% stop by turn 3: a strong next move one tap away keeps the first turns moving.

p4.text:
4 · Feel the change
A one-line delta chip after a beat ("Sasuke trusts you more"). Production runs the single-model storyteller, so this has to come from its output, not resolveIntent. Sparingly: one per beat, max.

p5.text:
5 · End on the cliffhanger, in the character's voice
The end card quotes the lead character, shows endings found (1 of 6), and asks for notification permission here, after the first cliffhanger, not at launch. The preview is the real message: in her voice, about 20 h after the run stops mid-scene, stopping after 2 ignored. Today there is no server push and "story waiting" is one generic line.

p6.text:
6 · Turn 10 is a wall: make it wait-or-pay
The free credits end at exactly turn 10, and day-0 play piles up at 10 and 15 turns. Equally engaged players who ran dry came back 5% of the time, against 23% for those with credits left. Lead with the wait (5 free turns in 3h 59m, plus a reminder), then the packs.

l1.text:
1 · Your turn
The latest run is a big card with its last line and Resume. Every row shows the beat, time since, and a dot when it is waiting on you.

l2.text:
2 · Tabs that collect
Playing · Saved · Finished · Endings. Endings found and relics make the library a collection, not a list, and a collection is a reason to replay.

l3.text:
3 · Never a dead end
Below the runs: "Players who loved Itachi also played". With one run (most players), today the screen is 90% empty.

tOnboarding.text: 5 · Onboarding: two questions, then the story

o1.text:
1 · One button, four best openers
The welcome shows the four best first stories and "Start a story". No sign-in buttons and no credit tooltip (that tooltip was OOC's).

o2.text:
2 · Pick vibes with pictures
Pick 3 tiles with art (Slow-burn romance, Dark mystery...). They choose the first story and feed Featured. OOC and Webtoon both ask; our current flow skips it.

o3.text:
3 · Name + age on one screen
Keeps the legal 18+ gate, cuts a screen. The button says what comes next; the name is used in the very next beat.

o4.text:
4 · Onboarding ends inside beat 1
38% of people who finish onboarding never start a story: half never open a story page, half open one and back out. So skip Discover and open the best opener for the picked vibes (here Good Morning Husband), with a default archetype and the name from step 3, so its setup page is skipped too.

o5.text:
5 · Ask for the account when there is something to save
After beat 3: Save Kai's story, +600 credits. Tied to progress the player now owns. Needs product sign-off: today guests cannot reach Library.

c1.text:
1 · A prompt, not an empty state
The tab opens on a text box and example chips instead of a centred paragraph and one button. (The builder flow itself: docs/create/ooc-teardown.md.)

c2.text:
2 · Remix a hit
Templates from trending tropes. A first world starts from a proven premise: the same tropes the story bot will target.

c3.text:
3 · Show creators winning
Your worlds with their play counts, and this week's top creators. Checking your numbers is its own reason to come back.

pr1.text:
1 · Who you are, up top
Avatar, level, streak and stats; settings move behind the gear. Today the profile is mostly a settings list.

pr2.text:
2 · Collections you can see filling
Endings and relics (0/34) as grids with locked silhouettes. The Relic vault is already the best-looking thing on this screen; give it more room.

pr3.text:
3 · The streak lives here too
The same 7-day strip as Home, so the daily habit has one consistent visual.

w1.text:
1 · Turns, not credits
Lead with "about 9 turns left" (600 credits at ~62 a turn on Vivid). Credits are an abstraction; turns are what people are buying, and the turn-10 wall is where they find out. The pack list already computes turns; promote them.

w2.text:
2 · The daily claim is a calendar
A 7-day strip with a day-7 bonus replaces the "Claim 300 daily credits" bar. Missing a day visibly costs something.

w3.text:
3 · Free ways to earn, above the packs
Tower, missions, invite. Players who earn come back, and payers come from players who come back.

w4.text:
4 · Packs as a grid
Two columns, turns as the headline, one Best value tag. The Pass keeps its own card on top.

t1.text:
1 · Tower is an event on Home
One card with today's countdown, the reward ladder in a line, and the best floor any player reached today. Built (docs/tower.md) but behind a flag in production, so there is no current screenshot.

t2.text:
2 · The lobby sells tomorrow
After a climb: floor reached, credits won, and "next climb in 14:12" with Remind me. One try a day is the whole point; the countdown is the retention mechanic.
